subject.title: add option for MCP apps support

question: Should OpenClaw host MCP Apps in core with a browser/gateway bridge, and what security/session contract must be satisfied before this draft can merge?
rationale: The feature changes the trust boundary by rendering MCP-provided HTML and letting iframe code call MCP tools/resources through gateway methods; automation cannot choose the permanent contract for persisted metadata, resource authorization, CSP, permissions, and restored sessions.

options.title: Require security fixes before merge
options.body: Keep the PR open but block merge until the sensitive metadata, resource size, CSP/permissions, and session-runtime concerns are fixed with focused tests and real Control UI proof.

options.title: Narrow to an experimental design branch
options.body: Keep the implementation as a draft/prototype while maintainers settle the MCP Apps host contract before accepting runtime/browser bridge code into core.

options.title: Accept opt-in trust model as-is
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly accept the current default-off risk, but that would leave capability persistence and resource policy gaps for users who enable the feature.

recommendation.title: Require security fixes before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but block merge until the sensitive metadata, resource size, CSP/permissions, and session-runtime concerns are fixed with focused tests and real Control UI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent and broad history on the affected MCP runtime, gateway authorization, Control UI, and canvas surfaces makes this the best available routing owner for the boundary decision.
